content.comment_body: I recently acquired 30 [article_no] [product_name] for a project at the National Museums Scotland. I'm looking to network them together, but I can't use Ethernet cables for each device. Therefore, I need a solution to connect them to the main corporate network via WiFi, which I'll provide using a basic wireless router connected to the corporate Ethernet network. There are adapters that convert Ethernet to WiFi, which could be used with each [product_name], as shown in this link: [url]. I have a few questions for the forum: 1) Has anyone networked [product_name] devices like [article_no] over WiFi? 2) If so, what hardware did you use for Ethernet-to-wireless conversion at the [product_name]? 3) Has anyone used Powerlink adapters that transmit Ethernet via the mains circuit? Thanks in advance for your help.

I've recently used a TP-link Wireless N nano router to enable WiFi connectivity on a project. It was inexpensive at £19.99 and functions well in our office setup; configuration as a wireless client was straightforward, just ensure the IP settings are correct. The only limitation is that it currently requires mains power, but I'm planning to use a 5V power supply so it can operate within the same panel.
I'm using a [article_no] connected to a standard router and I'm able to connect to the [product_name] via WiFi with no issues. From my experience, you don't need any special devices for this.

To [user_name]: Thank you for sharing your experience. If the nano router works successfully in client mode, all devices should function as clients to the main wireless router, so connecting all 30 units to the wireless network should be feasible. Have you tried operating more than one device in your configuration? I won't face issues with power supply since all my [article_no] units are designed for 240V. Thanks again for your input. To [user_name]: I appreciate your response, but I was asking about wireless communication between [product_name]s and the main network. Thanks for your reply nonetheless.

No problem, happy to assist. I'm just starting to work with [product_name] despite having experience with them, so I'm still learning. In response to your question, I haven't used more than one unit yet, but I'm planning to get the 3G version of the nano router today, which also works as a wireless client. Hopefully, I'll have two units operational shortly, including one on 3G – should be interesting to test.
Hello, could you clarify what you mean by 'just make sure the IP is correct'? Thank you in advance. [user_name]
I don't think you will receive an answer from [user_name]. Their last forum activity was on 3/2/2015.

analysis.insight_summary: A user asked for advice on creating a wireless network for 30 [product_name] devices due to physical cabling constraints. Multiple responses confirmed the feasibility of WiFi connectivity, recommending affordable consumer routers and WiFi adapters. While users have successfully networked individual devices, there was no confirmation regarding setups involving many devices simultaneously. Practical concerns included IP address configuration and appropriate power supplies for the routers.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for a dependable, scalable solution to connect all [product_name] devices wirelessly to a corporate network, hoping to confirm that commercial WiFi adapters will work for large deployments and seeking examples of similar implementations.
